commentary_target: This episode shows how GTA VI's reported and official wanted, phone-camera, social-media and money systems would punish four old-school crime methods (Capone's publicity, Corleone's family secrecy, a Yakuza boss's corporate cover, Shelby's information network), and argues which method survives and why.
note: The creator's second research report was available only as a summary (pasted text cut at Shelby); its tags are untrusted. Every claim below was checked against a page opened by the standards director on the date given, or is marked verified:false.

claims.text: GTA VI release: Rockstar's page says 'Coming November 19, 2026' (PS5, Xbox Series X|S); Take-Two's 2026-06-24 release gives the same date, $79.99 standard edition, pre-load Nov 12. Unreleased at the research date.
claims.label: official
claims.note: first-hand: rockstargames.com/VI and ir.take2games.com/node/32311, 2026-10-17

claims.text: Rockstar's page sets the game in 'Vice City, USA' within the state of Leonida ('criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida').
claims.label: official

claims.text: Rockstar's page names Jason and Lucia as the pair in the story ('Jason and Lucia's story').
claims.label: official
claims.note: surnames and backstory are not on that page

claims.text: Rockstar's page shows only the year 2026 (release and Newswire dates) and gives no in-story year.
claims.label: official
claims.note: the brief's '2025 setting' is therefore not established

claims.text: Rockstar's page names no regions of Leonida and no in-game social app, stock exchange or cryptocurrency.
claims.label: official
claims.note: absence on one page, not a denial

claims.text: Leonida is a fictional state based on Florida; reported regions include Vice City, Grassrivers, the Leonida Keys, Ambrosia, Mount Kalaga National Park and Port Gellhorn.
claims.label: community
claims.note: regions (Grassrivers, Leonida Keys, Ambrosia, Mount Kalaga, Port Gellhorn) are NOT on the Rockstar pages read; Wikipedia secondary lists them; treat as community/leak-derived, not official

claims.text: The setting satirises 2020s American culture; no specific year is given.
claims.label: official
claims.note: Wikipedia, first 100k characters of the article only

claims.text: Snapmatic is said (Wikipedia, secondary) to return as an in-game social app; Rockstar's pages do not confirm it. App names Snapmatic, Ryde Me, WAINK, Criminal Profile are unconfirmed.
claims.label: community
claims.note: do not state as official

claims.text: Rockstar has announced no in-game cryptocurrency (absence reported by a secondary summary).
claims.label: official
claims.note: crypto is unconfirmed for VI

claims.text: Press report: leaks of footage (2022 teapotuberhacker) and an August 2026 map and footage leak are described by a secondary source; a leaker-promoted meme coin was flagged by journalists as a possible scam.
claims.label: reported_leak
claims.note: named press outlets were not opened; usable only as 'reported' background, never as content; no leaked material is used (ER-17)

claims.text: The in-game stock market in GTA V is reached through an internet browser; this page names no exchange.
claims.label: official
claims.note: Wikipedia text read: 'The Internet lets players trade in stocks via a stock market'

claims.text: In GTA V, community guides describe LCN as the offline/single-player exchange driven by the player's own actions and BAWSAQ as driven by online players; neither is confirmed for VI. A link between the LifeInvader/Jay Norris assassination and LCN is NOT sourced.
claims.label: community
claims.note: source: search summary of fan guides (gtaboom, gamerhorizon, gamersheroes); fandom wiki returned 402; the bitget article was not opened and is low quality

claims.text: LifeInvader is GTA V's Facebook-style social network; not shown for VI.
claims.label: community
claims.note: not found in the pages read; nothing official for VI; speak only as 'GTA V's LifeInvader'

claims.text: Lester Crest is a GTA V character, described as a disabled hacker and Michael's old friend (voiced by Jay Klaitz); he is not shown in VI.
claims.label: official
claims.note: 'not shown in VI' is an absence claim, not verified

claims.text: Devin Weston is a GTA V billionaire venture capitalist and corporate raider; he is not shown in VI.
claims.label: official
claims.note: 'not shown in VI' is an absence claim, not verified

claims.text: Al Capone was convicted on five counts of income-tax evasion on 17 October 1931 and sentenced a week later to 11 years in federal prison.
claims.label: official
claims.note: encyclopedia page read first-hand; Britannica and FBI pages returned 403

claims.text: Capone was moved to Alcatraz in August 1934 and released from prison on 16 November 1939.
claims.label: official
claims.note: NPS and BOP pages gave no dates (NPS 404; BOP names him without dates)

claims.text: Capone died at home on Palm Island, Miami Beach, Florida, on 25 January 1947.
claims.label: official

claims.text: In March 1930 Capone was listed as 'Public Enemy #1' on the Chicago Crime Commission's widely publicised unofficial list.
claims.label: official
claims.note: Wikipedia Capone: March 1930 (a week after his release). The creator's report says 'early 1930'; April 1930 is also commonly cited but I found no source for April: use 'in 1930' in speech unless a primary-tier source is opened

claims.text: Capone sponsored a soup kitchen during the Depression (a photo caption dates one to February 1931).
claims.label: official
claims.note: Wikipedia: during the Depression, photo caption Feb 1931; the report's 'Nov 1930' is unsourced here: say 'during the Depression'

claims.text: IRS agent Frank J. Wilson, sent by Elmer Irey in May 1930, found a ledger line 'Frank paid $17,500 for Al' in fall 1930 and traced the bookkeeper (Leslie Shumway) who testified.
claims.label: official
claims.note: Wikipedia Frank J. Wilson, read first-hand. The Hawthorne Smoke Shop 1926 raid is not in that article (report's 'Hawthorne Hotel' looks wrong; search summaries say smoke shop): unverified. Indictment counts differ (Wilson article 23 counts, a search summary 22): do not give a number

claims.text: Newsreel coverage amplified Capone's public image.
claims.label: community
claims.note: no newsreel mention found in the pages read; unverified

claims.text: Genco Pura Olive Oil Company is the main legal front of Vito Corleone's syndicate.
claims.label: official
claims.note: fictional character page

claims.text: Vito refuses Sollozzo's offer to back heroin trafficking because the politicians and judges on his payroll would turn against him.
claims.label: official

claims.text: Vito dies of a heart attack on 29 July 1955 playing with his grandson in his garden.
claims.label: official

claims.text: The pursuit of casinos (Moe Greene stonewalling) is Michael Corleone's effort, not Vito's; the page does not name Nevada.
claims.label: official
claims.note: Nevada/Las Vegas setting comes from the films and is unverified here

claims.text: A phone camera that makes every act public plays the role the newsreel and press played for Capone.
claims.label: speculation
claims.note: inference from C-19, C-20; may also use Capone's 1930 'Public Enemy' listing

claims.text: The 1930s Shelby: elected MP in 1927 (constituency not confirmed; 'Birmingham South' not found); Series 5 runs 1929, Series 6 from December 1933; he uses information (Jessie Eden, false information fed to Billy Grade) but also arranges an assassination attempt on Mosley, murders the Barwell family and trades opium; no public 1930s gunfight is described.
claims.label: official
claims.note: Wikipedia Peaky Blinders and Tommy Shelby articles (first 100k characters); 'wins by data with no gunfire' is therefore our inference, not canon: a Shelby in public gunfights would be out of 1930s character, but 'never violent' would be wrong

claims.text: Take-Two's 2025-05-06 Trailer 2 release gave 'May 26, 2026' as the launch date; later releases moved it to November 19, 2026.
claims.label: official
claims.note: history of the date only

claims.text: Official trailer 1 shows civilians filming crimes on phones with short-form-video-style overlays.
claims.label: official
claims.note: the page confirms only the title 'Grand Theft Auto VI - Trailer 1'; the footage was not watched by me. The script may call 'filming civilians' OFFICIAL only after a person watches the trailer privately (ER-19) and records timestamps; until then it is 'reported in the creator's research'

claims.text: Rockstar's posting policy (updated 2025-01-10 per the report) allows non-commercial uses without spoilers, takes down leaked footage, isolated cinematics, spoiler edits, isolated in-game entertainment and cheat/mod-menu content, and says nothing about custom monetised 2D animation.
claims.label: official
claims.note: 503 on every attempt, not read first-hand; RK-02 stays REVIEW

claims.text: Illinois (765 ILCS 1075): post-mortem publicity right lasts 50 years, only for deaths after 1 Jan 1999, with exemptions for original films, books and other non-advertising works. Capone died in 1947, so this statute's post-mortem term does not reach him.
claims.label: official
claims.note: secondary summary; statute not read; not legal advice

claims.text: Florida Stat. 540.08: 40 years post-mortem; Tyne v. Time Warner (Fla. 2005) limited 'commercial purpose' to uses that directly promote a product or service and found a motion picture use not commercial. Capone died in 1947 (in Florida), beyond that term.
claims.label: official
claims.note: secondary summary; statute not read; not legal advice

claims.text: 'Burger Sohne AG' owns USPTO reg 1131459 'AL CAPONE' for tobacco goods; no estate enforcement found.
claims.label: community
claims.note: uspto.report company page 403; unverified

claims.text: Vito's details by novel chapter: Genco Pura (ch. 9), Sollozzo refusal (ch. 1), death in the tomato garden 1955 (ch. 31).
claims.label: community
claims.note: chapter numbers not opened: unverified; the film-character facts are C-23..C-25

claims.label: official

claims.text: Peaky Blinders: The Immortal Man, set a few years after the series finale, was released in cinemas on 6 March 2026 and on Netflix on 20 March 2026 with Cillian Murphy as Tommy.

claims.text: Boobie Ike, Brian Heder, Raul Bautista and Only Raw Records are not on Rockstar's pages; wanted system, money, crypto, laundering and legacy brands (eCola, Sprunk, LifeInvader, Bleeter, BAWSAQ, LCN, Lester, Weston) have nothing official for VI.
claims.label: community

claims.text: Our rating of Capone (opinion): Brutality 5, Adaptability 1, Tech-Savviness 1, Intimidation 4, Chaos Management 2. Reasons: public reputation for violence (opinion); his business and fame were tied to one city and to paper records (ledger line, C-21); no phone-era skills exist in the record. After the test (S30), our rating of Capone's Intimidation drops from 4 to 2: a public face leaves a trail (C-21, C-27).
claims.label: speculation
claims.note: The star values are the creator's; the reasons are ours. Said on screen and in narration as 'our rating'.

claims.text: Our rating of Vito Corleone, film-era Don (opinion): Brutality 2, Adaptability 2, Tech-Savviness 1, Influence/Networking 5, Strategy 4. Reasons: power from favours, judges and politicians and his refusal of the heroin deal (C-24); Genco Pura Olive Oil as the legal import front (C-23). After the test (S30), our rating of Vito's Influence drops from 5 to 3 once outside his circle (C-24, our inference).
claims.label: speculation
claims.note: Star values are the creator's; reasons from C-23, C-24.

claims.text: Our rating of the invented Yakuza boss (opinion, invented character): Brutality 4, Adaptability 4, Tech-Savviness 4, Discipline 5, Chaos Management 2. The character, his name and his corporate play are invented by us; 'the stock-market way of GTA V' refers to the stock market in GTA V (C-11). After the test (S30), our rating of the invented boss's Discipline goes from 5 to 4 (the street is not a boardroom).
claims.label: speculation
claims.note: Fully invented; no real group or real person; no Japanese-law claim is made (C-42 unverified).

claims.text: Our rating of Tommy Shelby, 1930s (opinion): Brutality 3, Adaptability 5, Tech-Savviness 5, Intelligence/Strategy 5, Influence 4. Reasons: information and politics (MP, false information fed to a rival) but also violence and opium trade (C-28); Tech-Savviness is relative to his era and our guess for a modern city. After the test (S30), our rating of Shelby's Strategy goes from 5 to 4 (certainty is a blind spot, our inference).
claims.label: speculation
claims.note: Star values are the creator's; reasons from C-28.

claims.text: The scenario is invented: four bosses from different eras placed in Leonida's Vice City. Rockstar gives no in-game year (C-04), so the year is our assumption.
claims.label: speculation
claims.note: Said plainly in the narration.

claims.text: The 'Florida-style' comic inserts are fully invented: no real incident, person or headline.
claims.label: speculation

claims.text: In GTA V, the wanted level (stars) rises when the police witness a crime.
claims.label: community
claims.note: general franchise knowledge, not opened in this run; spoken only as 'In GTA V'; nothing about the wanted level of the new game is stated (C-43).
